claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic as-cast microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has approximately 800 MPa yield strength and approximately 40% strain at lower temperatures.
The yield strength of undoped TiVNbTa falls to approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding approximately 0.05–0.1 wt% carbon and annealing TiVNbTa will precipitate MC-type carbides.
The resulting MC-type carbides will be fine, stable, and dispersed within the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
The carbide precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
The carbide precipitates will stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure at elevated temperatures.
Precipitation strengthening can mitigate the elevated-temperature strength deficiency of single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Carbon addition and annealing will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K above the reported baseline of approximately 330 MPa.
Carbon addition and annealing will enhance the creep resistance of TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
The modified alloy will maintain structural integrity under compressive loading to approximately 30% strain at temperatures up to 1273 K.
Excessive or poorly optimized carbon content may cause embrittlement, while unsuitable heat treatment may produce incomplete carbide precipitation.

contradictions.description: The reported baseline is an as-cast undoped alloy, whereas the proposed control is undoped but subjected to the same annealing treatment as the carbon-doped alloy. Annealing can itself change phase structure and properties, so this control is not necessarily equivalent to the stated 330 MPa as-cast baseline.

Enhanced creep resistance is claimed and included in the falsification rule, but the experiment specifies only compression to a fixed strain, hardness, and microscopy; it does not specify a creep test, hold time, stress, or creep-rate measurement.
